decisive_items: polygonal to short spindle-shaped cells formed small nests and sheets within dilated sinusoids without encapsulation
tumor cells exhibited clear cell borders, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, hyperchromatic nuclei, frequent mitotic figures
response.rationale: The young age, primitive basophilic multifocal cells with polygonal-to-spindle morphology, intrasinusoidal growth pattern, high-grade nuclear features, and local vascular invasion are most consistent with hepatoblastoma. Hepatocellular carcinoma is closer than benign lesions but less well explains the primitive/basophilic spindle-cell phenotype in this juvenile rat.

rejected.why: Hepatocellular carcinoma is possible but less specific for the primitive basophilic spindle-cell and younger-age presentation.
Vascular differentiation is not definitive; no clear endothelial-lined vascular channels are described.
No glandular/ductular differentiation to suggest cholangiocarcinoma.
Liver cell adenoma is too benign for invasion and mitotic activity.
Focal nodular hyperplasia is benign and unencapsulated with a different architecture.
Too broad and lacks the malignant/specific neoplastic diagnosis.
Malignant neoplasm is broadly applicable but lacks tumor-class specificity.
Hyperplasia does not match invasion, high mitotic activity, or malignant cytology.
Hepatic angiosarcoma remains possible but the described tumor is more hepatoblastoma-like than clearly endothelial.
Embryonal sarcoma typically has a more myxoid sarcomatous pattern; this tumor better fits hepatoblastoma morphology.
